name: Fluidstack
monetization: Assembles GPU capacity by leasing miner-owned datacenters (TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8) — with Google backstopping the leases — and delivers it to frontier labs, above all Anthropic.
description_md: Fluidstack is a London-founded GPU cloud that has become the AI buildout's distinctive intermediary: it signs decade-plus leases at miners-turned-AI landlords (TeraWulf Lake Mariner ~$9.5B up to ~$16B with extensions; Cipher Mining Barber Lake ~$3.8B base / ~$7.8B extended; Hut 8 River Bend $7.0B base / up to $17.7B), Google backstops billions of those lease obligations (taking warrants of ~14% in TeraWulf and ~5.4% in Cipher), and Anthropic anchors the capacity as end user. It is also Anthropic's development partner on the $50B US datacenter buildout announced Nov 2025 (Texas and New York first). Fluidstack's own balance sheet and valuation are not reliably public — an explicit data gap (SPEC §9.2b).
ai_monetization_md: Spread economics between long-term leases (obligations to landlords) and compute contracts with end users (Anthropic; also Google-facing arrangements, Meta and Mistral per press). The structure is credit-enhanced aggregation: Fluidstack itself is thin relative to the >$20B of base-term lease obligations it has signed, which is why Google's backstops are what make the leases financeable — landlord bonds (TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8 raised $15B+ against these leases) effectively price Alphabet's guarantee, not Fluidstack's credit. Reported financing: ~$830M Series A at ~$7.5B (Jan 2026) and mid-2026 talks at ~$18B — single-sourced secondary reports, UNVERIFIED.
ai_strategy_md: Move faster than hyperscaler procurement by renting the one asset miners already own — powered shells with grid interconnects — and matching them to frontier-lab demand: TeraWulf Lake Mariner (~360MW), Cipher Barber Lake (~207MW), Hut 8 River Bend (245MW), aggregating gigawatt-class capacity for Anthropic's $50B US program without owning land, power, or (mostly) chips. The Google relationship is the keystone: backstops de-risk the landlords' financing, and Google secures optionality over capacity in the TPU era. The open strategic question is whether Fluidstack graduates from credit-enhanced middleman to balance-sheet operator (an 'AI utility').
risk_notes_md: **Opacity:** no audited financials, no disclosed balance sheet; the ~$7.5B (Jan 2026) and ~$18B (talks, mid-2026) valuation figures are single-sourced secondary reports — UNVERIFIED, confidence low, recorded as such. **Structural thinness:** >$20B of base-term lease obligations vs undisclosed equity; absent the Google backstops the structure likely doesn't finance — meaning Fluidstack's viability is contingent on Alphabet's continued support and Anthropic's demand. **Two-sided concentration:** one dominant guarantor (Google) and one dominant end user (Anthropic); stress at either collapses the spread. **Flag:** the lease web is the canonical example of off-balance-sheet contingent risk migrating to a hyperscaler (see alphabet.json risk notes and the Google backstop observation there).
